breaker-boys-woodward.description: Breaker boys, Woodward Coal Mines, Kingston, Pa.
breaker-boys-woodward.collection: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.
breaker-boys-woodward.crop: cropped from the LOC master TIFF (4074x5191), x 2.5-97%, y 2-89%; the black glass-negative rim, the Detroit Photographic Co. blindstamp and the printed caption strip "81590 BREAKER BOYS, WOODWARD COAL MINES, KINGSTON, PA." are all outside the crop
breaker-boys-woodward.note: Detroit Publishing Co., c1900 - period-correct, NOT a Lewis Hine 1910-11 photograph. The negative number pencilled at top left of the plate reads mirror-reversed; that is normal for these plates (it was written on the glass side) and is NOT a sign that the scan is flipped — the printed caption and the railcar lettering in the frame both read correctly. Cropped out in any case.

breaker-boys-kingston.description: [Breaker boys, Woodward coal breakers, Kingston, Pa.]
breaker-boys-kingston.collection: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.
breaker-boys-kingston.crop: cropped from the LOC master TIFF (5149x4053), x 3-95.5%, y 4.5-95%; the black glass-negative rim and the pencilled negative number are outside the crop. NOT flipped - see note.
breaker-boys-kingston.note: Detroit Publishing Co., 1890-1901 - period-correct, NOT a Lewis Hine photograph. The pencilled number at top left of the plate reads mirror-reversed, which looks like an unflipped negative scan but is not: its companion plate 4a07285 (breaker-boys-woodward, same session, same hand, same corner) carries an equally reversed number while its printed caption and the railcar lettering inside the frame both read correctly. The numbers were written on the glass side. There is no legible text inside this frame, so there is no positive evidence of reversal and the image has been left as the Library holds it.
